([[Moundville, Alabama]]) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2017–2021) | highlights = * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], ''[[Sporting News|SN]]'' ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] (2021) * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2021) * SEC Defensive Player of the Year (2021) * 2× SEC All-Defensive Team (2020, 2021) }} '''Herbert Jones''' (born October 6, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. He earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a senior in 2021, when he was also named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]]. ==High school career== Jones started playing [[varsity team|varsity]] basketball as a seventh-grader for Sunshine High School in [[Newbern, Alabama]], where his father served as the head coach. He played alongside his older brother, Walter Jr., and helped his team reach the Class 1A state finals in 2015, before the school closed.{{cite web |last1=Champlin |first1=Drew |title=Small town standout Herb Jones has big basketball dreams |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/10/hale_county_standout_herb_jone.html |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 4, 2016}} For his junior season, Jones transferred to [[Hale County High School]] in nearby [[Moundville, Alabama]], following his father, who was an assistant coach.{{cite web |last1=Tsoukalas |first1=Tony |title=How a brotherly bond has always fueled Alabama freshman Herbert Jones |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/how-a-brotherly-bond-has-always-fueled-alabama-freshman-herbert-jones |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 16, 2021 |date=November 17, 2017}} As a senior, he averaged 16.6 points, 8.2 rebounds and four assists, earning Class 4A Player of the Year honors.{{cite web |last1=Chandler |first1=Joey |title=Jones, Ford win Class 4A Player of the Year honors |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/sports/20170404/jones-ford-win-class-4a-player-of-year-honors |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=April 4, 2017}} Jones led Hale County to the 4A state championship, its first-ever state title.{{cite web |last1=Estwick |first1=Gary |title=Kaddell Perry, Herb Jones lead Hale County past Monroe County for 1st state title |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/kaddell-perry-alabama-commit-herb-jones-lead-hale-county-boys-to-first-ever-class-4a-crown/ |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=March 3, 2017}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web |last1=Champlin |first1=Drew |title=Hale County guard Herb Jones commits to Alabama |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/10/herb_jones_hale_county_alabama.html |website=AL.com |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 6, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman at Alabama, Jones averaged 4.2 points and 3.5 rebounds per game. He drew a single-season program record 23 charges.{{cite web |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=Herbert Jones 'means a tremendous amount' to Tide basketball |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Herbert-Jones-means-a-tremendous-amount-to-Crimson-Tide-program-124468527/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=November 9, 2018}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 6.4 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Herb Jones' Offensive Development Could Be X-Factor for Crimson Tide Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/herb-jones-offensive-development-could-be-x-factor-for-crimson-tide |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=October 26, 2020}} On January 29, 2020, during a game against [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], Jones suffered a fractured left wrist and underwent surgery three days later. He returned to action on February 12 while wearing a cast on his wrist.{{cite web |last1=Byington |first1=Alex |title=How Alabama's one-handed Herb Jones showed 'warrior' approach returning to the floor against Auburn |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2020/02/13/how-alabama-basketballs-one-handed-herb-jones-showed-warrior-approach-return-vs-auburn/4751983002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 13, 2020}} In his next game, after three days, Jones recorded six points and 17 rebounds in an 88–82 win over LSU. Late in the game, he made two free throws using only his right hand, due to his injury.{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Christopher |title=Alabama Still Getting 'Goosebumps' From Epic Herb Jones Free Throws |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-goosebumps-herb-jones-free-throws |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 18, 2020}} As a junior, Jones averaged 7.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game and was a [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Defensive Team selection. He declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] before withdrawing and returning to college.{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Alabama Basketball's Herbert Jones Returning For Senior Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-basketballs-herbert-jones-returning-for-senior-season |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=June 3, 2020}} At the close of the 2020–21 regular season, Jones was named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year by the league's coaches.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/31030484/2021-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|title=2021 SEC Men's Basketball Awards Announced|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 11.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. On April 8, 2021, Jones declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his extra year of college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Martin |first1=Tyler |title=Alabama Basketball’s Herb Jones Officially Declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabamas-herb-jones-officially-declares-for-2021-nba-draft |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 26, 2021 |date=April 8, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | '''35''' || 13 || 21.2 || .408 || .269 || .500 || 3.5 || 1.4 || 1.3 || .6 || 4.2 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | 34 || 29 || 21.1 || .422 || .286 || .495 || 3.5 || 2.0 || .9 || .6 || 6.4 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | 27 || 26 || 26.5 || '''.484''' || .071 || .625 || 6.4 || 2.3 || 1.3 || .7 || 7.9 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]] | 33 || '''33''' || '''27.3''' || .446 || '''.351''' || '''.713''' || '''6.6''' || '''3.3''' || '''1.7''' || '''1.1''' || '''11.2''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 129 || 101 || 23.8 || .441 || .288 || .604 || 4.9 || 2.2 || 1.3 || .8 || 7.3 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Jones is the son of Walter Sr. and Verlander Jones. He was born with [[hemolytic anemia]].{{cite web |last1=Burger |first1=Kyle |title=Alabama basketball player Herbert Jones fighting blood disorder since birth |url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/alabama-s-herbert-jones-fighting-since-birth/26542223 |website=[[WVTM-TV]] |access-date=January 18, 2021 |date=February 26, 2019}} His older brother, Walter Jr., played college basketball for [[Texas–Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|Texas–Rio Grande Valley]] and [[Alabama A&M Bulldogs basketball|Alabama A&M]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://rolltide.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/herbert-jones/6827 Alabama Crimson Tide bio] {{Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Jones, Herbert}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball players]] [[Category:All-American college men's basketball players]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Alabama]] [[Category:People from Greensboro, Alabama]] [[Category:People from Northport, Alabama]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Small forwards]]
